title: Ground-field retagging preserves the full tower purity comparison
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, an algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$, and put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-pur-conventions, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes with structural maps $a_X,a_Y$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth separated $k$-morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $\sigma:k\simeq k$ fix $k_0$, and write $T^{\langle\sigma\rangle}$ for the same underlying scheme $T$ with structural map $\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)\circ a_T$, for $T=X,Y$, and $f^{\langle\sigma\rangle}$ for the same underlying morphism between these retagged schemes.

Use the ordinary derived categories of varying-coefficient strict towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers] and their uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], with the tower adjunctions $F_f=Rf_{!,\bullet}\dashv G_f=f^!_\bullet$ of [det-sp-tower-gluing], and the natural purity maps $\gamma_{f,\bullet}(K_\bullet):f_\bullet^*K_\bullet(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}G_fK_\bullet$ of [det-sp-tower-gamma]. The tensor products and twists in this construction are ordinary tower tensor products and the levelwise Tate twists [def-weil-derived-tensor, def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Identify the small pro-etale sites and coefficient systems by the identity of underlying schemes, identify $F_f$ and $F_{f^{\langle\sigma\rangle}}$ using the same underlying compactification, and identify their right adjoints by the unique counit-preserving adjunction isomorphism. Then for every $K_\bullet$ in the indicated constructible finite-Tor category, under these identifications of sources and targets,
$$\gamma_{f^{\langle\sigma\rangle},\bullet}(K_\bullet)=\gamma_{f,\bullet}(K_\bullet)$$
as an equality of morphisms in the ordinary derived category of towers, retaining the quotient-coefficient transitions. No normalization of $K_\bullet$ is required.

source.place: Steps 1–3 on coefficient towers; invariance of the tensor-map transpose under ground-field retagging (explicit auxiliary comparison)

proof.text: Retagging changes only the structural maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$. The underlying schemes, the morphism $f$, and the chosen compactification $X\to\overline X\to Y$ are unchanged. Thus the identified small pro-etale ringed sites give exactly the same strict tower categories, exact pullback functors, and termwise tensor operations. This is an identity of the abelian tower categories of [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], so it induces an identity on complexes and on their ordinary derived categories, retaining the quotient transitions. The Tate sheaves of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] are unchanged: on an object $U$ their roots of unity are the same units satisfying $u^{\ell^r}=1$, with the same power transition maps. The compactification construction of $F_\bullet$ is likewise the same underlying functor. Identify the right adjoints by the stipulated counit-preserving isomorphism; [det-sp-tower-gluing](2) supplies its uniqueness and the Hom bijection. This argument uses the identity of the entire tower construction, not faithfulness of finite evaluations on derived morphisms.

source.place: Step 1, tower purity comparison under the identity of underlying sites and compactification

proof.text: The reviewed auxiliary comparison [lem-pur-orientation-ground-field-retagging] gives, under exactly the same underlying-site and counit-preserving adjoint identifications, the equality of normalized tower orientations a_{f^{\langle\sigma\rangle},\bullet}=a_{f,\bullet}, including all quotient-coefficient transition maps. Hence the orientation factor in the definition of the purity map is unchanged.

source.place: Step 1, normalized tower orientation under ground-field retagging

proof.text: For $K_\bullet$ in the stated constructible finite-Tor category, [det-sp-tower-gamma](2) defines $t_K$ as the adjoint transpose of $C_K:F_\bullet(f^*_\bullet K_\bullet\otimes^L\omega_{f,\bullet})\to K_\bullet$, where $C_K$ is inverse projection formula followed by $1\otimes\varepsilon_\bullet$ at the coefficient unit. The projection transformation is the compactification construction of [def-exchange-projection]: the direct-image projection map is the transpose of the pullback-tensor comparison followed by the ordinary direct-image counit, and it is followed by the extension-by-zero tensor comparison. Retagging leaves each of these constructions unchanged on the identical underlying sites and compactification of Step 1; the same applies to their tower construction used in [det-sp-tower-gamma](2), before any evaluation. The projection transformation is natural in the $\omega$ input, so the counit-preserving identification $\rho:G_{\mathrm{retag}}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_f$ also identifies $C_K$ for the two choices of $\omega=G(1)$. Explicitly, the two maps $t_{f,K}\circ(1\otimes\rho_1)$ and $\rho_K\circ t_{\mathrm{retag},K}$ have the same transpose: apply $\varepsilon_{f,K}\circ F_\bullet(-)$, use $\varepsilon_f\circ F_\bullet(\rho)=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{retag}}$, and the just-identified projection composite. Injectivity of the Hom bijection of [det-sp-tower-gluing], or the adjunct-counit identity [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity], makes these two maps equal. Step 2 gives $\rho_1\circ a_{\mathrm{retag}}=a_f$. Composing with $1\otimes a$ and the common twist reassociation therefore gives $\rho_K\circ\gamma_{\mathrm{retag}}(K_\bullet)=\gamma_f(K_\bullet)$, exactly the asserted equality under the stipulated identifications. The domain is the full constructible finite-Tor tower category in [det-sp-tower-gamma](2), so no normalization assumption is used.

split_report.summary: Audited the tower purity retagging statement against the tower gluing and tower gamma interfaces. No new node is needed: the reviewed sibling lem-pur-orientation-ground-field-retagging supplies the required equality of normalized tower orientations, while det-sp-tower-gamma defines purity as the unique adjoint transpose of the projection-formula map. The identity-on-underlying-sites and same-compactification hypotheses make every other factor identical, so the purity maps agree for every constructible finite-Tor tower without normalization.
